newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products-Gulf gasoline up, Harbor weakens.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products-Gulf gasoline up, Harbor weakens.

text.p: U.S. Gulf Coast gasoline differentials firmed by late Thursday, while New York Harbor reformulated gasolines showed some weakness, though outright prices came under pressure as the NYMEX continued its slide.
Conventional gasoline differentials firmed, helped by renewed refiner buying on the U.S. Gulf Coast, traders said, though that activity appeared to be covering of short positions.
On the NYMEX, July gasoline fell 0.60 cent to settle at 59.82 cents and July heating oil dropped 0.84 cent to finish at 53.32 cents.
U.S. GULF COAST
Prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline differentials jumped higher, offsetting most of the drop on the NYMEX, as refiners re-entered the market as buyers, traders said.
That action did not appear to be the result of any refinery outages in the region, according to players, but rather those refiners covering committments in the market.

Prompt regular M1 gasoline changed hands at 1.00 cent under the July NYMEX, up about 0.50 cent from late Wednesday levels. M1 barrels for delivery at the end of June traded at 2.75 cents under the July contract, up about 0.25 cent on the day.

Prompt heating oil barrels inched higher as a schedulng deadline at the end of the day forced shorts to buy up barrels. Prompt material traded at 2.10 cents under the July NYMEX price, up about 0.15 cent on the day.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Reformulated gasoline hovered at lower levels in the Harbor as ample supply continued to dog prices.
"We are well supplied here between imports and production," said a dealer.

After reformulated 87-octane gasoline traded at 0.15 cent over NYMEX July gasoline in the morning, down from 0.50 to 0.75 cent over on Wednesday, it continued to be talked between 0.10 and 0.25 cent over in the afternoon.
Conventional also slipped, with offers at 2.00 cents under the July NYMEX versus 1.75 under on Wednesday.

Traders attempted to talk reformulated premium 93-octane D2 gasoline higher at 9.00 cents over the NYMEX, but no deals were cited and 8.50 cents over the July contract was seen as a more realistic level.
Heating oil had found comfort zone slightly below NYMEX, with talk continuing between even with the July contract and 0.25 cent under after a deal was done at 0.10 cent under.
MIDCONTINENT
U.S. midcontinent refined oil products markets remained calm late Thursday afternoon as many players stepped out of the fray to let the NYMEX selloff run its course, traders said.
"It's been real quiet with the NYMEX doing its thing," said one trader.
Any month low sulphur diesel in Group Three changed hands at 3.40 cents over July futures, with prompt barrels heard offered at 4.00 cents over.
Group gasoline differentials held onto the strength they picked up late Wednesday, with prompt barrels pegged at between 4.25 and 4.50 cents over July futures.
Prompt unleaded in Chicago stood at between 2.25 and 2.50 cents over July NYMEX.
Premium grades were steady in both centers.
